text: Before anything had a name, there was an ocean of milk, and on it, a serpent with no end.
On its coils, Vishnu rests: the preserver, with Lakshmi at his feet, the goddess of good fortune.
His name is often read as the one who pervades everything. The sky and the ocean are his colour.
asr: His name is often red as the one who pervades everything. The sky and the ocean are his color.

text: He holds a conch, a discus, a mace, and a lotus, and he rides on Garuda, king of the birds.
Garuda is the enemy of every serpent, and still he carries the god who sleeps on one.
asr: Garyuda is the enemy of every serpent, and still he carries the god who sleeps on one.

text: When the world falls out of balance, Vishnu comes down to set it right. Once, he came as a dwarf.
Vamana asked the great king Bali for a small gift: only as much land as he could cover in three steps.
asr: Vemana asked the great king Bali for a small gift: only as much land as he could cover in three steps.

text: The king laughed, and agreed. And the dwarf began to grow.
With his first step, he covered the earth.
With his second step, the heavens.
There was nowhere left for the third. So Bali bowed, and offered his own head.
In the far south, the city of Thiruvananthapuram takes its name from him: the city of the endless serpent.
asr: In the far south, the city of Tiruvananthapuram takes its name from him: the city of the endless serpent.

text: In its great temple, Padmanabhaswamy, he lies at rest, so long that he can only be seen through three doors.
asr: In its great temple, Padmanapaswami, he lies at rest, so long that he can only be seen through three doors.

text: In the Bhagavad Gita, as Krishna, he makes a promise: whenever goodness declines, I come again, age after age.
And some say he is closer than that. In a Himalayan river in Nepal, pilgrims gather black stones marked with spirals.
asr: And some say he is closer than that. In a Himalayan river in Nepal, pilgrims gather black stones marked with spirals.

text: They are ammonites, sea creatures turned to stone some hundred and fifty million years ago, honoured as Vishnu himself: the shaligram.
asr: They are Ammonites. Sea creatures turned to stone some hundred and fifty million years ago, honored as Vishnu himself. The Shalagram.

text: An ocean, a step, a stone. The one who pervades everything, in a line without an end.
